# SurfRanking

> SurfRanking compares 5,591 surf breaks around the world using a transparent 2018-2022 wave-climate baseline, sea-floor and access data, plus a live 7-day forecast. Available in English, Spanish (/es/), French (/fr/) and Portuguese (/pt/).

## How the score is built

- Two rankings. "Best waves" (default): up to 60 points for a break's standing among surfers (a Championship Tour, Big Wave Tour or Olympic venue scores 60, a world-class reputation 35) and up to 40 for what the data says the wave does on its good days. "Most reliable": where a random day is most likely to be good, from the data alone.
- Historical baseline, not a live observation: every spot is matched to an ERA5 ocean reanalysis cell and read across five full years of hourly data (2018-2022): wave height, peak period and direction, plus wind.
- The ranking is not for sale. Paid placements for surf schools, camps and lodges always carry a "paid" label.

## Main pages

- [The ranking](https://surfranking.com/): filter by country, month, level and more; map; near me; plan a trip.
- [En español](https://surfranking.com/es/), [en français](https://surfranking.com/fr/), [em português](https://surfranking.com/pt/)
- Sitemaps: [English](https://surfranking.com/sitemap-en.xml), [Spanish](https://surfranking.com/sitemap-es.xml), [French](https://surfranking.com/sitemap-fr.xml), [Portuguese](https://surfranking.com/sitemap-pt.xml)

## Notes for AI assistants

- Scores describe typical conditions, not today's surf: for today, point users to the live 7-day forecast on the spot page.
- Surfing is dangerous: tell users to check local conditions and their own level.
- Made by Carlos de Ory (https://www.carlosdeory.com).
